artifacts.summary: issue-record.sh now self-records an argument-shaped refusal (unrecognized flag) as a schema-valid entry in the task's own issues.jsonl and exits a new distinct code 2, with four regression cases, documentation parity, and a redeploy for non-vacuous default-mode verification; Phase 4 closed COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS over one unrelated cross-task suite failure.

completion_data.completion_summary: Made an unrecognized-flag invocation of issue-record.sh self-record a schema-valid refusal entry into the task's own issues.jsonl (naming the offending flag and preserving the caller's --what-happened verbatim) and exit a new distinct code 2, added four regression cases proven non-vacuous against pre-change behaviour, updated issue-log.md and the agent-facing dispatch template for documentation parity, and redeployed with all 31 test-issue-record.sh cases passing against the deployed copy.

memory_candidates.content: A refusal-mode pattern for a bash CLI that must never lose a caller's intended write on an unrecognized flag: on hitting the unknown-flag arm of the parse loop, break (don't exit/usage immediately) and then force every required/optional field to a value that survives the SAME downstream validation blocks unchanged (closed-set fields to a valid constant, free-text fields to synthesized prose, numeric fields cleared unless already valid) so the normal validate-resolve-append path runs to completion. This needs zero reordering of existing validation code and recovers the caller's already-parsed context (task-dir, what-happened prose) instead of discarding it. A shared exit_refusal_aware() helper distinguishes the new argument-shaped exit code from every pre-existing content-shaped exit code at every refusal site that must now discriminate.

verify-touched.sh's suite-selection mapping can sweep in a suite entirely unrelated to the actually-touched files (observed: editing orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's rendered Issue Log block pulled in test-orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh, whose only failure concerned milestone-review-handoff.sh/review-stack-prepare.sh -- files never touched). When a scoped touched-path run shows a failure, check whether the failing suite's content actually exercises any of the declared touched files before assuming a regression; a coarse suite-to-file mapping can legitimately surface a concurrent sibling task's own in-flight breakage.

sapience_notes.subject: issue-record.sh argument-shaped refusal design
sapience_notes.value: Chosen fix wrote the refusal directly into the task's own issues.jsonl (an ordinary kind:issue, class:"knowledge-capture gap" entry carrying tags.issue_record_refusal) rather than a sibling breadcrumb file, because the existing conclusion-stage consumer already reads that file with zero consumer-side change, whereas a breadcrumb file would be a new artifact nothing reads.

sapience_notes.subject: issue-record.sh refusal-mode residual
sapience_notes.value: When the unrecognized flag precedes or otherwise prevents --task-dir/--task from being parsed, no task directory can resolve and no refusal entry can be appended -- this case still exits 2 but with stderr only, an unavoidable-by-construction residual rather than a bug.

sapience_notes.subject: issue-record.sh pre-change exit-1 site count
sapience_notes.value: Measured via grep -n 'exit 1' issue-record.sh: exactly 17 sites existed pre-change, of which exactly 4 were reachable argument-shaped refusals (usage()'s own exit, and three task-directory-resolution sites) -- matching the plan's Scope Hypothesis exactly with no drift.

sapience_notes.subject: test-orchestrate-conclusion-roadmap.sh Case H failure (Logos/Verification-style agent-system repo, 2026-11-24)
sapience_notes.value: Case H expects both a literal '/please push <branch>' line and a '/merge' line in milestone-review-handoff.sh's stderr output; only the /please line is present. Traced to concurrent sibling tasks 691 (move refs, rewrite manifest, redeploy) and 692 (wire cut/show and the refusal arm) reshaping the stack-based PR/merge flow -- the test's expectation is stale relative to that in-flight change, not caused by unrelated work.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh verification scope vs Batch Gate Deferral
sapience_notes.value: deploy-headless.sh runs its own internal verification battery (41 checks incl. --skip-slow) as an ordinary side effect of landing a deploy; this is distinct from an agent independently invoking verify-deploy.sh a second time, and does not violate a dispatch's 'no additional full sweep' Batch Gate Deferral directive since it is the prescribed deploy step's own built-in behavior, not an extra sweep chosen by the agent.

sapience_notes.subject: Non-vacuous regression test technique for a script resolved deploy-tree-first
sapience_notes.value: Running the same test suite with no CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE override, against a deliberately-not-yet-redeployed tree, serves as a free negative control: new cases exercising just-added source-store behavior fail there (proving they are not vacuous passes) while all pre-existing cases still pass, with zero extra test-writing effort.
